{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZeMC0w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDFYbs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 95, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified browser-local outbound TELNET journey from MAIN 7", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `98ce69d477bae7887fdbde3a96287a1ce2641d70`, MAIN `7 インターネット` offers only `1 NetNews`. Users cannot experience the documented transition from PC-VAN into a separate remote server.

November 1996 documentation explicitly describes entering PC-VAN and using TELNET to log into a server for remote mail access. This is a material missing service journey, extending the bounded NetNews scope rather than correcting an implementation regression.

## Expected outcome

Provide this keyboard journey entirely within the browser:

`MAIN or index → 7 Internet → 2 TELNET → select the bundled host → automatic demo login → remote MAIL → list/read original letters → remote logout → TELNET directory → Internet directory → actual entry parent`

Use one fictional host, `mail.demo.example.invalid`, and an automatically displayed fictional account. Bundle two short original Japanese letters illustrating ordinary late-1996 correspondence. Keep this remote mailbox visibly distinct from PC-VAN electronic mail.

Use a deliberately small reconstructed command subset:

- TELNET directory: `OPEN mail.demo.example.invalid`, `LIST`, `HELP`, `BACK`, `MAIN`.
- Remote shell-like view: `MAIL`, `LOGOUT`, `HELP`, `BACK`, `MAIN`.
- Remote mailbox: `LIST`, `READ number`, `LOGOUT`, `HELP`, `BACK`, `MAIN`.

These are authored demonstration controls, not authenticated PC-VAN gateway syntax or an emulation of a particular UNIX mail program. Include a concise local-demo indication at entry and fuller provenance in existing Settings/About and research documentation. Do not request credentials or make network connections.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction judgment

Sources inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- [Internet Magazine, November 1996, printed page 232](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf) describes entering a commercial service including PC-VAN, then using TELNET to log into a separate server for mail access. It distinguishes remote UNIX operation from graphical mail clients. Confidence is high for the documented capability and service boundary. It supplies no complete PC-VAN gateway command sequence, destination menu or remote mail commands.
- [Internet White Paper 1996, printed pages 110–111](https://iwparchives.jp/files/pdf/iwp1996/iwp1996-ch04-01-p110.pdf) explains remote login and reports bidirectional TELNET in the PC-VAN comparison column. Confidence is moderate to high in this contemporary comparison. Subscriber figures are labeled January 1996; this does not establish an exact feature activation date. Text/table extraction was inspected; no new page-image comparison is claimed.
- [Internet Magazine, April 1995, printed page 105](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199504-104-bbs.pdf) explicitly says PC-VAN then permitted incoming TELNET but not outgoing connections. Confidence is high within that earlier snapshot. Preserve this chronological distinction: the earlier restriction cannot define late-1996 behavior. Its illustrated ASAHIネット menus cannot supply PC-VAN commands.
- The [retrospective MAIN reproduction labeled circa 1996](https://www.paradisearmy.com/doujin/pasok3pc-van.htm) places Internet at MAIN 7. Confidence is high in the displayed reproduction; historical authenticity and revision dates remain provisional. It does not authenticate a secondary TELNET menu.

Focused searches for PC-VAN TELNET commands, destination selection and termination recovered no qualifying target-year gateway sequence. Incoming-access guides and later service comparisons do not resolve those controls.

Judgment: capability and the remote-mail use case are sufficiently supported for this increment. Selector 2, host/account, login display, prompts, command subset, mailbox contents, returns and any timing are category D reconstruction. Exact historical controls remain an open research question, not a completion gate. Reuse existing terminal reveal behavior without adding a new timing subsystem.

### Implementation and existing evidence

- `src/netnews.ts:renderInternetDirectory` renders only NetNews. `src/navigation.ts` owns Internet dispatch, parent stacks and service contexts; its `internet-directory` case accepts only selector 1.
- `src/main.ts` calls `TerminalCommands.submit` before navigation. `src/commands.ts` intercepts application shortcuts and composition commands. Route remote commands deliberately so they cannot invoke local mail, forum or conference composition, OSL downloads or OLT participation. Preserve existing application shortcuts.
- `src/connection.ts` forwards navigation contexts. Keep TELNET views outside `forum`, `mailContext`, `netNewsContext`, `isConference`, `isOlt` and community-content requirements. No storage schema or migration is needed for bundled read-only examples.
- `tests/netnews.spec.ts` currently treats Internet selector 2 as invalid in controller and production journeys. Update those specific expectations while preserving NetNews coverage. Existing controller tests and `tests/terminal-helpers.ts` provide production keyboard, restore, backup, literal-text and protected-record comparison patterns.
- Update README, existing Settings/About content and `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md`, including statements that currently exclude TELNET from the implemented subset.

Live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs. TELNET Issue history returned [#81](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/81), whose NetNews scope explicitly excluded TELNET; no equivalent pending handoff was found. Lexical history searches are incomplete and inventory can change.

[PR #94](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/94) matches the baseline merge. Its description and `docs/validation.md` report 38 focused and 331 full-suite passing checks, configured type checking/build and implementation/publication review. These are existing Coordinator records, not checks performed by this research graph or validation of this proposal.

Scope excludes real TELNET transport, arbitrary hosts/ports, password entry, a general shell, remote composition/sending, inbound PC-VAN Internet mail, persistent remote read markers, new AI activity, downloads and other Internet services.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] MAIN 7 retains `1 NetNews` and adds working `2 TELNET`. The TELNET directory lists the single bundled host and the exact supported OPEN command. Opening it displays an automatic fictional login and a distinct remote prompt. Anonymous and registered users can complete the journey without consent, model preparation or credential entry.
- [ ] Remote MAIL lists exactly two original letters with stable numbers, fictional correspondents, subjects and complete Japanese bodies. Use `.invalid` addresses and original content. Do not copy archive messages, identities or images, or identify the fictional host as a recovered historical destination.
- [ ] `READ number` opens only a valid bundled letter; `LIST` restores the complete remote mailbox. `HELP` redisplays the current view without changing selection. `BACK` follows letter → mailbox → remote shell → TELNET directory → Internet directory → actual MAIN/index parent. `LOGOUT` from any remote view ends only the remote session and returns to the TELNET directory. `MAIN` clears remote state and returns directly to MAIN. Repeated reads, logout and re-entry create no duplicate parents or stale selections.
- [ ] Missing or unsupported hosts, malformed OPEN commands, invalid/unsafe/out-of-range numbers and unsupported remote commands produce contextual responses without changing the active view or protected records. Do not resolve arbitrary destinations. Verify remote `MAIL`, `READ`, `LOGOUT`, `WRITE`, `REPLY`, `INBOX`, `DOWNLOAD` and OLT-like input cannot trigger another service or log out of PC-VAN accidentally.
- [ ] Existing global Settings/About, log, backup, import/reset and AI controls retain their ownership and safeguards. Returning from Settings/About restores the same TELNET view. Reload begins with normal application entry rather than restoring a remote login. Preserve existing reset/restore invalidation and terminal input behavior.
- [ ] Bundle the remote host/account/mail outside IndexedDB and community backups. The journey creates no members, local mail, read confirmations, forum/conference/OLT records, resident memory, consent or scheduling changes. Preserve restored-empty collections. Ordinary session command history, activity bookkeeping and terminal logs may continue; do not claim total backup equality where those normally change.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright/controller coverage for the complete journey, both MAIN/index entry paths, both letters, invalid hosts/commands/numbers, every return/escape path, repeated visits and NetNews availability afterward. Include production keyboard journeys in anonymous restored-empty and registered worlds, protected-record comparisons with automatic activity paused, Settings/About returns, reload, existing import/reset safeguards, literal Japanese output/log export, simulated composing-Enter protection and usable input/scrolling at 320px. Observe no external requests, DNS/connection attempts, model loading or external handoffs caused by TELNET interaction.
- [ ] Document URLs, inspection date, historical scope, confidence and category D choices. Explicitly distinguish the 1995 inbound-only restriction from 1996 outbound evidence, PC-VAN controls from remote-server controls, and remote bundled mail from PC-VAN mail. Keep routine terminal output concise and truthful about local demonstration behavior.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test` before merge; the existing Playwright configuration performs TypeScript checking and the production build. Preserve functional, storage/import/reset, consent, mail privacy, IME and terminal pacing/skip coverage. Use existing tooling without real-model execution or a new framework. Review the complete diff, documentation links and whitespace, and record actual results and failures accurately.

## Optional validation

Compare the reconstruction with a subsequently recovered dated outbound PC-VAN TELNET session. Additional browser-engine or native-IME checks are optional; human or hardware confirmation is not a completion gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. This scope can be verified against local production assets before merge.
